Fit a mixture regression model in which the relationship between an outcome and its predictors differs across latent classes

Source: R/mixture-regression.R
mixture_regression.Rd

mixture_regression() fits a mixture of class-specific regressions, in which the relationship between an outcome and its predictors differs across latent classes. Classes can differ in outcome level, in predictor associations or in trajectory over time. Regression parameters and class probabilities are estimated jointly by maximum likelihood.

Predictors in formula describe variation within classes; covariates in membership describe who belongs to which class. A coefficient may be shared by every class (common). Class membership can belong to each row or to every row of a unit (class_level); with a time predictor and shared membership the classes are trajectories, and random adds within-class variation around them (a growth mixture model). Outcomes can be Gaussian, binomial, Poisson, negative binomial or ordinal.

Usage

mixture_regression(
  formula,
  data,
  n_classes,
  family = c("gaussian", "binomial", "poisson", "negative_binomial", "ordinal"),
  id = NULL,
  class_level = c("observation", "group"),
  n_group_classes = 1L,
  common = NULL,
  membership = ~1,
  group_membership = ~1,
  variance = c("varying", "equal"),
  n_starts = 10L,
  max_iter = 1000L,
  tol = 1e-08,
  min_variance = 1e-06,
  seed = NULL,
  missing = c("error", "omit"),
  select_start = c("likelihood", "converged"),
  vcov_type = c("observed", "robust", "opg", "none"),
  weights = NULL,
  random = NULL,
  random_covariance = c("varying", "equal", "proportional"),
  random_diagonal = FALSE,
  cluster = NULL,
  residual_correlation = c("none", "ar", "brownian"),
  residual_time = NULL
)

Arguments

formula

A model formula outcome ~ predictors. Factors, interactions and offset() are supported.

data

A data frame.

n_classes

Number of regression classes; a positive integer.

family

The distribution of the outcome within a class:

  • "gaussian" (default): a continuous outcome, identity link;

  • "binomial": a binary outcome or counts of successes and failures, logit link;

  • "poisson": a count outcome, log link;

  • "negative_binomial": a count outcome more dispersed than a Poisson, log link;

  • "ordinal": an ordered categorical outcome, cumulative logit link.

See Families for the accepted outcome codings.

id

NULL (default), or the column identifying the units (persons, schools) the rows belong to.

class_level

What a class is assigned to:

  • "observation" (default): each row has its own class, so two rows of the same unit can be in different classes;

  • "group": all rows of a unit share one class, so the classes are kinds of units. It needs id.

See Nesting.

n_group_classes

Number of second-level group classes (default 1, none). For class_level = "observation" with id, classes of the units: a unit's class sets the class probabilities of its rows. For a growth mixture with cluster, classes of the clusters. More than one needs id.

common

Predictor terms whose coefficients are shared by every class, as names ("age") or a one-sided formula (~ age). Each term must appear in formula; the intercept cannot be shared. NULL (default) lets every coefficient differ between classes.

membership

Covariates of class membership, a multinomial logit with the first class as reference: names or a one-sided formula (~ 1, the default, for none). Row-level under "observation", constant within units under "group".

group_membership

Covariates of the group class, as names or a one-sided formula (~ 1, the default, for none); constant within the units that carry group classes (the id units, or the clusters under cluster).

variance

For the Gaussian and negative-binomial families (an error when given with the others), whether the classes share their residual variation:

  • "varying" (default): each class has its own residual standard deviation (or negative-binomial dispersion);

  • "equal": one value shared by all classes, so the classes differ only in their coefficients.

n_starts

Number of random starts (default 10), besides one start built from the residuals of a pooled regression. Each start runs up to 50 EM iterations; the better half (at least two) continue to convergence.

max_iter

Maximum EM iterations per start (default 1000).

tol

Convergence tolerance (default 1e-8), per row: EM stops when a step changes the log likelihood by no more than tol times the number of rows of positive weight.

min_variance

Floor on a Gaussian residual variance, as a fraction of the outcome's variance (default 1e-6). A start in which a class's residual variance reaches the floor is excluded from selection. In a growth mixture the same floor bounds each random effect's conditional variance; a random-effect variance at the floor is kept and warned about.

seed

Optional integer seed; when given, the caller's random-number state is restored on exit.

missing

What to do with rows that have a missing value in any variable the model uses:

  • "error" (default): stop, saying how many rows are affected;

  • "omit": drop those rows and fit the complete ones, with a latents_rows_dropped warning saying how many were dropped.

select_start

Which start is reported:

  • "likelihood" (default): the start with the highest log likelihood, whether or not it converged;

  • "converged": the start with the highest log likelihood among those that converged, or among all starts when none converged.

Starts in which a class emptied or a residual variance reached its floor are set aside under either rule.

vcov_type

The covariance matrix of the estimates stored with the fit, from which the standard errors and confidence intervals are taken:

  • "observed" (default): the inverse of the observed information;

  • "robust": the sandwich estimator, clustered on the independent units;

  • "opg": the outer product of the scores;

  • "none": no covariance matrix is stored, which saves the time of computing it during the fit. A table that needs standard errors then computes them when it is requested (from the observed information; the sandwich for a weighted fit).

A weighted fit uses "robust" by default and accepts only "robust" or "none".

weights

Name of a numeric column holding a sampling weight per independent unit (per row without id, per unit with it): pseudo maximum likelihood with robust standard errors. A unit of weight zero is absent from the fit and every criterion but keeps its row and posterior. NULL (default) weights every unit equally.

random

NULL (default), or the random effects within classes: names such as "time" (a random intercept and a random slope on time) or "intercept", or a one-sided formula such as ~ 1 + time (~ 0 + time for a slope alone). Giving random fits a growth mixture model; it needs the Gaussian family, id and class_level = "group". See Growth mixture models.

random_covariance

With random, how the covariance matrix of the random effects differs between classes:

  • "varying" (default): one matrix per class;

  • "equal": one matrix shared by all classes (lcmm::hlme(nwg = FALSE));

  • "proportional": a shared matrix times a class-specific scale, the last class's scale being one (nwg = TRUE).

random_diagonal

With random: FALSE (default) estimates the covariances between the random effects; TRUE sets them to zero, so the random effects are uncorrelated (idiag = TRUE in lcmm).

cluster

Column grouping the units of id into clusters, such as schools, for the multilevel growth mixture model (with random): each cluster belongs to one of n_group_classes group classes, which sets the trajectory-class probabilities of its persons. The clusters are the independent units of the likelihood, the standard errors and the BIC. NULL (default) has no cluster level. Not combined with weights. See Growth mixture models.

residual_correlation

With random, how the residuals of one unit are correlated over time:

  • "none" (default): independent residuals;

  • "ar": a continuous-time autoregressive process is added, with covariance sd^2 * exp(-rate * |t - s|) between times t and s (lcmm::hlme(cor = AR(time)));

  • "brownian": Brownian motion is added, with covariance sd^2 * min(t, s) (cor = BM(time)).

The process is shared by the classes. One the data cannot separate from the residual variance or the random effects stays on its bound, warns, and has no standard error. These fits refine one class placement from the model without the process; n_best_replicated is NA, and "starts" reports the correlated fit rather than the initialization's replication count.

residual_time

Numeric time column of the residual process; default the first numeric variable in random, otherwise in the predictors. Brownian motion needs non-negative times. Given without residual_correlation, it is an error.

Value

A fitted model of class latents_mixture_regression, or of class latents_growth_mixture when random is given. Printing it shows the fit, the classes and the coefficients. get_results() returns its tables by name, among them:

  • "coefficients" (also as.data.frame(fit)): one row per class and term, with the estimate, standard error, confidence limits and p-value;

  • "classes": the share of each class, the number of rows assigned to it, its average posterior probability and its residual standard deviation;

  • "membership": the coefficients of the membership covariates;

  • "fit": the log likelihood, number of parameters, AIC, BIC, SABIC, ICL and entropy;

  • "assignments": each row's (or unit's) most likely class and posterior probabilities;

  • "starts": the log likelihood and convergence of every start.

A regression mixture also has "fitted", "classification", "groups" and "group_classes"; a growth mixture has "random" (the random-effect variances), "random_effects", "trajectories" and "individual". predict(), plot() (and plot_trajectories(), plot_coefficients()), summary(), coef(), vcov(), confint(), logLik() and nobs() apply. The within-class coefficients are conditional associations under the specified model, not causal effects; check the starts table and the classification diagnostics before reading substance into the classes.

Conditions

Errors: latents_bad_argument for an argument value or combination that is not accepted (for example class_level = "group" without id, variance with a family that has none, or random without class_level = "group"); latents_bad_data for a variable that data does not have or an outcome the family cannot take; latents_missing_data for missing values under missing = "error"; latents_not_identified for the models listed under Families; latents_no_valid_start when a class emptied or a variance collapsed in every start; latents_unsupported_weights for a weighted fit asked for a vcov_type other than "robust" or "none", or combined with cluster.

Warnings: latents_unconverged when the reported start did not converge; latents_degenerate_start when some starts were set aside; latents_rows_dropped for rows left out under missing = "omit"; latents_random_boundary for a random-effect variance at its floor.

Nesting

id = NULL

Each row is an independent unit.

class_level = "group"

All rows of a unit share a class, the regression mixture for repeated measures (flexmix(y ~ x | id)); a unit's likelihood is the product of its rows' densities.

class_level = "observation" with id and n_group_classes >= 2

Each row has its own class, and a group class of its unit sets the class probabilities. With n_group_classes = 1, id clusters the robust standard errors and is the unit of weights.

Growth mixture models

With repeated measurements (id, class_level = "group") and time in formula, the classes are trajectories: without random effects a latent class growth model, with random a growth mixture model. For unit i in class k,

$$y_i = X_i \beta_k + Z_i b_i + e_i, \quad b_i \sim N(0, G_k), \quad e_i \sim N(0, \sigma_k^2 I),$$

with Z the design of random. Random effects need the Gaussian family, id, class_level = "group" and, for a random intercept, repeated rows in at least some units. With residual_correlation, e_i also carries the autoregressive or Brownian process over residual_time.

With cluster, persons are nested in clusters and each cluster belongs to a group class h that sets the trajectory-class logits of its persons (a class-specific intercept with shared covariate slopes):

$$L = \prod_j \sum_h \omega_h \prod_{i \in j} \sum_k \pi_{k|h} f_k(y_i)$$

group_membership names cluster-level covariates of the group class; the group classes are in get_results(fit, "group_classes") and "clusters". With n_group_classes = 1 the fit is comparable by BIC with fits that add group classes.

Families

"gaussian": identity link, a residual standard deviation per class or one shared. "binomial": logit link; the outcome is 0/1, logical, a two-level factor (second level the success) or cbind(successes, failures). "poisson": log link, offset() honoured. "negative_binomial": log link, NB2 (variance mu + alpha * mu^2) with a dispersion per class or one shared; a dispersion estimated at zero is the Poisson limit, reported with a warning and no standard error.

"ordinal": a cumulative-logit (proportional-odds) regression within each class, \(P(Y \le c \mid x, k) = \mathrm{plogis}(t_{kc} - x'\beta_k)\), with ordered thresholds per class in place of the intercept and the sign convention of MASS::polr(): a positive slope raises the probability of a higher category. The outcome is an ordered factor, a factor (levels in order) or whole numbers; the categories are those observed, at least two. The formula keeps its intercept, which the thresholds replace. Thresholds appear in the coefficient table as "threshold:<lower>|<upper>", and exp_estimate of a slope is a cumulative odds ratio. The class mean of an ordinal outcome (fitted values, trajectories) is the expected category score with categories scored 1 to C; predict(type = "probabilities") gives the category probabilities.

Identification. Call the thing that carries a class the unit: a row, or an id group under class_level = "group". An ordinal mixture whose units have one outcome each and no predictors is not identified (a mixture of categorical distributions is itself one) and is refused. A binary mixture with one trial per unit, and an ordinal one with one outcome per unit and two categories, are refused too: whether such a model is identified depends on the covariate design, which the package does not assess. Give each unit several outcomes (class_level = "group") or, for binomial, counts with more than one trial per row. A single-level ordinal mixture is also refused when it has more free parameters than the distinct covariate patterns can identify. Repeated binary or ordinal outcomes without predictors must also have enough distinct response-count patterns to identify the class parameters. A growth model is refused when its random-effects and residual covariance components cannot be separated by the observed designs. With class-specific residual variances, two common waves do not identify an unrestricted random intercept and slope covariance. A diagonal covariance can be identified there, as can proportional class covariances with a shared residual variance.

Unused factor levels in membership and random-effects formulas are dropped before fitting. In output tables, an identifier whose name conflicts with a result column is prefixed with id_ or cluster_ (for example, an id = "class" column is returned as id_class, beside the latent class). A numeric suffix is added if that name is also occupied.

Every refusal and warning is a classed condition; latents-conditions lists them.

See also

enumerate_regressions() to compare numbers of classes; plot_trajectories(), plot_coefficients() and, for fits that classify persons, plot_classification().

Examples

fit <- mixture_regression(score ~ hours, data = study_hours, n_classes = 2,
                          n_starts = 3, seed = 1)
fit
#> Mixture of gaussian regressions: 2 classes (one class per row)
#> score ~ hours
#> 900 rows | log likelihood -3144.0073 | BIC 6335.63 | entropy 0.443
#> Converged: TRUE | iterations: 53 | best likelihood reached by 2 of 2 completed starts (4 run)
#> 
#> Classes
#> 
#> Class    Share  Expected  Rows assigned  Avg. posterior  Residual SD
#> -------  -----  --------  -------------  --------------  -----------
#> Class 1  0.564    507.71            573           0.789         5.24
#> Class 2  0.436    392.29            327           0.829         6.89
#> 
#> Regression coefficients (95% CI)
#> 
#> Class    Term       Estimate          95% CI      p
#> -------  ---------  --------  --------------  -----
#> Class 1  Intercept     34.36  [32.95, 35.77]  <.001
#> Class 1  hours          4.57  [ 4.36,  4.77]  <.001
#> Class 2  Intercept     54.90  [52.76, 57.04]  <.001
#> Class 2  hours          0.81  [ 0.48,  1.14]  <.001
#> 
#> Every table: get_results(x, what = ), e.g. "classes", "membership", "fit", "assignments".
as.data.frame(fit)
#> Regression coefficients (95% CI)
#> 
#> Class    Term       Estimate          95% CI      p
#> -------  ---------  --------  --------------  -----
#> Class 1  Intercept     34.36  [32.95, 35.77]  <.001
#> Class 1  hours          4.57  [ 4.36,  4.77]  <.001
#> Class 2  Intercept     54.90  [52.76, 57.04]  <.001
#> Class 2  hours          0.81  [ 0.48,  1.14]  <.001
get_results(fit, "classes")
#> Classes
#> 
#> Class    Share  Expected  Rows assigned  Avg. posterior  Residual SD
#> -------  -----  --------  -------------  --------------  -----------
#> Class 1  0.564    507.71            573           0.789         5.24
#> Class 2  0.436    392.29            327           0.829         6.89

# One class per student, several rows per student:
by_student <- mixture_regression(score ~ hours, data = study_hours, n_classes = 2,
                                 id = "student", class_level = "group",
                                 n_starts = 3, seed = 1)
get_results(by_student, "fit")
#> Model fit
#> 
#> Family          gaussian
#> Nesting         group
#> Classes         2
#> Group classes   1
#> Observations    900
#> Groups          150
#> Parameters      7
#> Log likelihood  -3177.76
#> AIC             6369.52
#> BIC             6390.60
#> SABIC           6368.44
#> ICL             6451.31
#> Entropy         0.708
#> Smallest class  46.9%
#> Converged       yes

# \donttest{
# Students nested in schools, each school in one of two group classes:
schools <- mixture_regression(score ~ wave, growth_schools, n_classes = 2,
                              id = "student", class_level = "group",
                              random = "wave", random_covariance = "equal",
                              cluster = "school", n_group_classes = 2,
                              n_starts = 2, seed = 1)
get_results(schools, "group_classes")
#> Group classes: trajectory classes within each
#> 
#> Group class    Class    Probability     SE  Share of clusters  Clusters
#> -------------  -------  -----------  -----  -----------------  --------
#> Group class 1  Class 1        0.842  0.024              0.544        22
#> Group class 1  Class 2        0.158  0.024              0.544        22
#> Group class 2  Class 1        0.233  0.030              0.456        18
#> Group class 2  Class 2        0.767  0.030              0.456        18
